pairs.subject: long-form-reading-surface
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Article.tsx:76 The editors show a written article as section cards: a heading, a word count and the section's lead, inside a scrolling workspace region. None of the subject's terms (IntersectionObserver, scroll-margin, slugify, location.hash, href="#) appear under app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/, so there is no contents panel, no heading anchor, no fixed-chrome offset and no scroll-spy for the subject to govern.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Article.tsx:77 Headings have no id and nothing links to them. Sections are found by data-section through keyboard selection, which is the technique's own 'nothing ever links to them, skip ids' case.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Editors.module.css:4 Nothing pinned waits on an anchor jump. The only sticky rule in the context is a horizontal lane label in Cut.module.css (left:0), so there is no top budget to own.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Article.tsx:30 The highlight (data-on) is an operator selection walked by keys and scrolled into view. It is not a current-section indicator measured from scroll position. No IntersectionObserver or progress bar exists.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:142 Picking a candidate in the rail swaps the beat document in place, but it is a list-detail comparison walked by item keys, not navigation between articles. The technique's own exclusion says moving focus to a heading there would be a jolt.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/page.tsx:33 The section list arrives prepared in the server-loaded view and the client never parses it. With no contents panel and no id-placing renderer, there is no second consumer for the structure to be shared with.
